::: {#thm-deviance-drop}

#### The drop in deviance is the likelihood ratio statistic

Let $D_0$ be the [null deviance](#def-null-deviance) and $D$ the [deviance](#def-deviance) of a logistic regression with $q$ predictors besides the intercept.
Then the [likelihood ratio statistic](intro-MLEs.qmd#def-lrt-stat) of $H_0$: all $q$ slopes are zero is

$$
\lrstat = D_0 - D.
$$

:::

::: proof
In the notation of the [likelihood ratio statistic](intro-MLEs.qmd#def-lrt-stat), the unrestricted MLE $\hthml$ is the fitted coefficient vector $\hvcoef$, and $\hparam_0$ is the fit of the intercept-only model that $H_0$ imposes.
Then $\llikf{\hthml} = -D / 2$ and $\llikf{\hparam_0} = -D_0 / 2$.
Substituting both into the definition gives $\lrstat = 2 \paren{-D/2 + D_0/2} = D_0 - D$.
:::
